issues.legal_issue: A technical institution that shifts to a new site without completing the required approval procedure may have its approval withdrawn and may be refused approval to operate at the new site.
material_facts: The institution moved to new premises before receiving prior approval from the technical education regulator and without obtaining the required no-objection certificates.
It had no occupancy certificate for the new premises and had not established the required ownership or registered lease interest in the land.
The applicable site-change procedure required specified land documents, approvals and compliance with infrastructure requirements.
The regulator withdrew approval, and the High Court declined to interfere.
issues.conclusion: The withdrawal of approval and refusal to approve operation at the new site were lawful, and the High Court's decision was not interfered with.
issues.legal_principle: The AICTE Act, particularly Sections 10(1)(k) and 10(1)(p), authorizes the AICTE to grant approval and inspect technical institutions. Clause 9.22 of the Approval Process Handbook required compliance with the prescribed site-change procedure, including the necessary no-objection certificates and acceptable land documents. Recognition conditions and regulations must be strictly complied with; the right to establish an institution does not itself confer a right to recognition or affiliation, as stated in Unni Krishnan, J.P. v. State of Andhra Pradesh and reaffirmed in Medical Council of India v. Madhu Singh and Ranjan Purohit v. Rajasthan University of Health Sciences.

rule.if: approval_withdrawal_appeal and institution_shifted_without_prior_approval and (required_land_interest_absent or occupancy_certificate_absent or required_no_objection_certificates_absent)

predicates.approval_withdrawal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the withdrawal or refusal of approval for a technical institution.
predicates.institution_shifted_without_prior_approv: The institution moved its operations to a different site before obtaining the regulator's approval for the move.
predicates.required_land_interest_absent: The institution had not established the land ownership or qualifying registered lease required for the new site.
predicates.occupancy_certificate_absent: The institution had not obtained an occupancy certificate for the new premises.
predicates.required_no_objection_certificates_absen: The institution had not obtained the required no-objection certificates from the relevant authorities.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an approval decision and the institution moved without prior approval while a required land, occupancy or no-objection condition was unmet, the withdrawal or refusal of approval for the new site may be upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Annual approval expressly limited to an institution's approved location does not amount to approval for a different site.
material_facts: The institution had received annual approvals that specified its original site and required it to operate only from the approved location.
The institution had applied to shift to new premises, but the application had not been finally determined.
The institution began operating at the new premises without a decision approving the change.
issues.conclusion: The annual approvals for the earlier academic years did not constitute express, implied or deemed approval of the new site.
issues.legal_principle: Approval must be granted through an appropriate decision made with due diligence and in accordance with the prescribed procedure; it cannot be inferred from approvals expressly tied to another location. Clause 9.22 of the Approval Process Handbook governed changes of site. The Court also applied the principle in Unni Krishnan, J.P. v. State of Andhra Pradesh that recognition is not automatic or a formality and must follow the prescribed conditions.

predicates.approval_location_appeal: The proceeding challenges whether an institution was approved to operate at a particular site.
predicates.prior_approval_identified_a_specific_sit: The prior approval identified the location from which the institution was permitted to operate.
predicates.institution_operated_at_a_different_site: The institution operated at another location without receiving a decision expressly approving that change.

issues.definition: Where prior approval specified one site and the institution operated at another without an express site-change decision, the prior approval does not authorize operation at the different site.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not substitute its assessment for that of a specialist educational regulator unless the regulator has acted arbitrarily, capriciously or contrary to law.
material_facts: The regulator's decision concerned compliance with technical-education approval requirements, including site conditions and infrastructure.
The institution had shifted sites without completing the prescribed approval procedure and had outstanding deficiencies.
The High Court found no basis to require approval at the new site, and the Supreme Court found no ground to disturb that decision.
issues.conclusion: The regulator's decision was not subject to judicial substitution on these facts, and the Court declined to interfere with the refusal to grant approval.
issues.legal_principle: Courts ordinarily defer to specialist bodies on educational policy and academic matters, but may intervene to interpret, apply or enforce law and where an expert body's powers are exercised arbitrarily, capriciously or impermissibly. The Court relied on Adarsh Shiksha Mahavidyalaya v. Subhash Rahangdale, State of Tamil Nadu v. Adhiyaman Educational & Research Institute, Bharathidasan University v. All India Council for Technical Education, and AICTE v. Surinder Kumar Dhawan.

predicates.expert_approval_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an approval decision made by a specialist educational regulator.
predicates.decision_involves_specialist_educational: The decision concerns technical standards, infrastructure or other matters requiring specialist educational assessment.
predicates.arbitrary_or_unlawful_regulatory_action: The regulator acted arbitrarily, capriciously or in a manner impermissible under the governing law.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a specialist educational assessment and the regulator did not act arbitrarily or unlawfully, the court does not replace the regulator's assessment with its own.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory approval and admission schedules for technical education must be strictly followed and cannot be varied by the authorities.
material_facts: The applicable approval regulations contained a schedule for processing applications, and the Court found that the schedule had statutory backing.
The Court considered the approval and admission timelines together and prescribed a revised, fixed admission schedule to avoid uncertainty and prejudice to students.
The institution sought relief after the applicable admission deadline had passed.
issues.conclusion: The approval and admission schedules are mandatory, the fixed dates declared by the Court must be strictly followed, and no authority may vary them.
issues.legal_principle: The schedule made under the AICTE Act, Section 23(1), and the 1994 AICTE approval regulations has statutory backing and is mandatory rather than directory. Admission schedules must be strictly complied with, as held in Unni Krishnan, J.P. v. State of Andhra Pradesh, Medical Council of India v. Madhu Singh, and Ranjan Purohit v. Rajasthan University of Health Sciences. The Court declared its revised approval and admission schedule to be law and prohibited variation by any authority.

predicates.technical_education_approval_or_admissio: The proceeding concerns approval of a technical institution or admission to a technical education course.
predicates.binding_approval_or_admission_schedule_a: A binding schedule governs the approval or admission process at issue.

issues.definition: When a binding schedule applies to a technical education approval or admission proceeding, its deadlines must be followed and cannot be varied.

issues.legal_issue: An approval granted after the final approval deadline cannot operate for the current academic year.
material_facts: The Court fixed a final date for approval decisions and required admission materials to include only institutions approved by the applicable deadline.
It directed that even an approval granted by an appellate authority after the final approval date would not operate for the current academic year.
issues.conclusion: An institution approved after the final approval deadline may not be included for admissions in the current academic year.
issues.legal_principle: The Court's fixed approval and admission schedule, declared to be law, requires approval decisions to be made by the prescribed deadline. The Court relied on the mandatory character of the AICTE approval schedule under the 1994 regulations and the need for strict adherence to admission schedules, including the principles in Medical Council of India v. Madhu Singh and Ranjan Purohit v. Rajasthan University of Health Sciences.

predicates.technical_education_admission_proceeding: The proceeding concerns admissions to a technical education course for an academic year.
predicates.approval_granted_after_final_approval_de: The institution's approval was granted after the final date fixed for approval decisions.

issues.definition: If approval is granted after the final approval deadline for an academic year, it cannot support admissions for that year.

issues.legal_issue: The technical education regulator must communicate identified deficiencies promptly and provide a defined period for their correction during approval processing.
material_facts: The regulator had failed to deal promptly with the institution's site-change application and had not clearly resolved deficiencies identified during inspection.
The Court directed that applicants be informed of shortcomings or defects within a specified short period and be given a period to remove them.
The Court also required the approval process to be transparent and fair.
issues.conclusion: During approval processing, the regulator must communicate identified shortcomings or defects promptly, and the applicant must be given a defined period to remedy them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the statutory approval timetable under the AICTE Act and the 1994 approval regulations and directed that approval processing be transparent, fair and timely. It further directed the regulator to communicate deficiencies within the specified period and to set a period for their removal.

predicates.technical_institution_approval_applicati: An institution has applied for approval or for approval of additional seats.
predicates.regulator_identifies_application_deficie: The regulator or its inspection process has identified shortcomings or defects in the application or institution.

issues.definition: When an approval application has identified deficiencies, the regulator must communicate them promptly and set a period for their correction.

issues.legal_issue: A regulator's unjustified approval decisions and failures in processing may warrant costs and recovery from the responsible officials when they jeopardize students.
material_facts: The regulator granted annual approvals while the site-change application remained pending and despite an expert inspection identifying inadequacies.
It later issued a show-cause notice and withdrew approval, requiring students to move colleges during their studies.
The Court found the regulator's handling irresponsible and held that it had jeopardized the students' academic careers.
issues.conclusion: The regulator was ordered to pay costs, recoverable from the salaries of the officials responsible in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: A public educational regulator is required to act responsibly and in accordance with the approval process; the Court may impose costs for an irresponsible and erroneous exercise of its functions that causes serious prejudice to students.

predicates.technical_approval_administration_disput: The proceeding concerns the regulator's handling of approval for a technical institution.
predicates.regulator_granted_approval_despite_known: The regulator granted approval despite an inspection or other information identifying deficiencies.
predicates.regulator_handling_jeopardized_students: The regulator's handling of the matter placed students' academic progress or careers at risk.

issues.definition: When a regulator grants approval despite known deficiencies and its handling jeopardizes students, costs may be imposed and recovered from the responsible officials.

issues.legal_issue: When withdrawal of an institution's approval disrupts enrolled students' studies, the regulator and affiliating university must arrange alternative placements and ensure completion of their academic courses.
material_facts: Withdrawal of approval prevented the institution from continuing to operate as approved.
Students had been admitted to the institution, and shifting them to other colleges during the academic year would disrupt their studies.
The Court directed that the students be reallocated to recognized and affiliated colleges and that necessary extra classes be held to complete their courses.
issues.conclusion: The students must be reallocated to recognized and affiliated colleges, and the regulator and university must ensure completion of their academic courses within the remaining period of the academic year, including through extra classes if needed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated student welfare as requiring protective arrangements when an institution's approval is withdrawn and directed the regulator and affiliating university to ensure that affected students can complete their academic courses.

predicates.institution_approval_withdrawn: Approval for the institution has been withdrawn or the institution can no longer continue operating as approved.
predicates.enrolled_students_academic_courses_disru: Students enrolled at the institution face disruption to their academic courses as a result.

issues.definition: If approval is withdrawn and enrolled students' courses are disrupted, the students must be reallocated and their courses completed.
